test_title: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-I (Held On : 19 April 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: An article is sold at a profit of 13(1)/(4)%. Had it been sold for Rs. 76.70 more, the profit would have been 16(1)/(5)%. 50% of the cost price of the article (in Rs.) is:
solution:
**Calculations:**

Let the cost price be Rs 100.

SP for 131over 4% profit = Rs 100 + 13.25 = Rs 113.25

SP for 161over 5% profit = Rs 100 + 16.20 = Rs 116.20

Difference in profit = Rs 116.20 - Rs 113.25 = Rs 2.95

**Difference Cost Price**

Rs 2.95 100

Rs 76.70 x

⇒ x = 76.7times 100 over 2.95 = Rs 2600

∴ **50% of the cost price is Rs 1300.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

Difference of profit% of (16(1)/(5) - 13(1)/(4)) = (16.2 - 13.25) = 2.95% makes the difference of price of Rs. 76.70

So, 2.95% → 76.70, then 100% → (76.70/2.95 × 100) = Rs. 2600 (which is the CP)

Now, 50% of the cost price is = 2600/2 = Rs 1300.
